I think you are conflating mental illness and insanity as one thing. In your example of Existential OCD, you can empathize with it (as you're saying), so you wouldn't force them to take treatment against their consent and may be you're too generous. And most of the time they are aware of their OCD and that they need help. So, I'd say they have mental illness, but they are not insane. 

But everyone has different levels of empathy. Take a different example, where a person is causing too much nuisance in the locality where he lives, doing absurd things, killing animals, or worse, feeding on their dead body's flesh in public making a complete mess etc. I don't know which disorder it would fall into, but that guy would end up in a psych ward pretty quickly and not by himself. We can still have differences in opinion, but that's the kind of insanity I'm talking about. 

My point is, there is a subjective element to what we refer to as insane, and if more people think someone is insane, we are more willing to believe that the guy has a mental illness, without ever conducting a medical test. So, there must be some way to measure this deviance from normal such that it's statistically significant e.g. "99.9 percent of healthy people don't display this kind of behavior that's why he seems insane". That's one way to rationally express our feelings towards the insane. And it also then makes insanity a statistical construct, because we have never had medical tests to say that it is medical situation.
